title.raw: 卷104 自序 Volume 104: Author's Preface

sentences.zh: 漢初，魏無知封高良侯，子均，均子恢，恢子彥。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han, Wei Wuzhi was enfeoffed as Marquis of Gaoliang; his son was Jun, Jun's son Hui, and Hui's son Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Han dynasty, Wei Wuzhi was made Marquis of Gaoliang; from him came Jun, from Jun came Hui, and from Hui came Yan.

sentences.zh: 彥子歆，字子胡，幼孤有志操，博洽經史，成帝世，位終鉅鹿太守，[2]仍家焉。

translations.literal: Yan's son Xin, courtesy name Zihu, orphaned young yet resolute in will and conduct, thoroughly versed in the classics and histories; in the reign of Emperor Cheng he ended his career as Administrator of Julu, [2] and the family settled there.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's son Xin, styled Zihu, lost his father early but possessed strong character. Well read in the classics and histories, he served during Emperor Cheng's reign and ultimately became Administrator of Julu, [2] where the family established its home.

sentences.zh: 歆子悅，[3]字處德，性沉厚有度量，宣城公趙國李孝伯見而重之，以女妻焉。

translations.literal: Xin's son Yue, [3] courtesy name Chude, of deep and steady nature with great forbearance; Xuan Cheng Gong Li Xiaobo of Zhao State saw him and held him in esteem, giving him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Xin's son Yue, [3] styled Chude, was grave, steady, and broad-minded. Li Xiaobo, Duke of Xuan Cheng in Zhao, took a liking to him and gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 位濟陰太守，以善政稱。

translations.literal: He held the post of Administrator of Jiyin, famed for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Administrator of Jiyin and won renown for his effective administration.

sentences.zh: 悅子子建，字敬忠。

translations.literal: Yue's son Zijian, courtesy name Jingzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's son Zijian, styled Jingzhong.

sentences.zh: 釋褐奉朝請，累遷太尉從事中郎。

translations.literal: Upon leaving the cloth he became Attending Counselor at Court; through successive promotions he rose to Attendant of the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: After beginning his career as Attending Counselor at Court, he was promoted repeatedly until he became Attendant to the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 初，世宗時平氐，[4]遂於武興立鎮，尋改為東益州。

translations.literal: Initially, in Emperor Shizong's time the Di were pacified, [4] and a garrison was established at Wuxing, soon changed to Eastern Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during Emperor Shizong's reign the Di were subdued, [4] and a military post was set up at Wuxing, which before long became the province of Eastern Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 其後鎮將、刺史乖失人和，羣氐作梗，遂為邊患，乃除子建為東益州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereafter the garrison commander and regional inspector lost harmony with the people; the Di tribes caused obstruction and it became a border affliction, so Zijian was appointed Regional Inspector of Eastern Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later the garrison commanders and provincial inspectors failed to maintain good relations with the people. The Di rose in obstruction and the region became a border trouble spot, so Zijian was appointed governor of Eastern Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 子建布以恩信，風化大行，遠近清靜。

translations.literal: Zijian spread favor and trust; moral transformation was greatly practiced, and far and near were quiet and clear.
translations.idiomatic: Zijian governed with kindness and integrity. His influence spread widely, and peace returned to the region near and far.

sentences.zh: 正光五年，南、北二秦城人莫折念生、韓祖香、張長命相繼構逆，僉以州城之人莫不勁勇，同類悉反，宜先收其器械。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhengguang, city people of Southern and Northern Er Qin—Mo She Niansheng, Han Zuxiang, and Zhang Changming—in succession raised rebellion; all agreed that the people of the provincial capital were without exception stalwart and brave, their kindred all having turned rebel, and that their weapons ought first be confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Zhengguang, Mo She Niansheng, Han Zuxiang, and Zhang Changming led successive rebellions among the townspeople of the two Qin provinces. Officials agreed that the capital's inhabitants were fierce fighters and that their clansmen had already risen in revolt, so their arms should be seized first.

sentences.zh: 子建以為城人數當行陳，盡皆驍果，安之足以為用，急之腹背為憂，乃悉召居城老壯曉示之；

translations.literal: Zijian held that the city people were those who were due to serve in the ranks, all of them fierce and resolute; if pacified they would suffice for use, but if pressed, trouble front and rear would be the concern; he therefore summoned all old and young dwelling in the city and explained this to them;
translations.idiomatic: Zijian reasoned that these city dwellers were men slated for military service—every one of them tough and battle-ready. Treat them well and they could be enlisted; push them hard and they would become a danger on every side. So he called together all the elderly and able-bodied residents and explained his thinking to them.

sentences.zh: 并上言諸城人本非罪坐而來者悉求聽免。

translations.literal: And in a memorial he requested that all city people who had come not because of criminal conviction be granted exemption and released.
translations.idiomatic: He also petitioned the throne to exempt and release all those city dwellers who had been sent there for reasons other than criminal punishment.

sentences.zh: 肅宗優詔從之。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong graciously issued an edict acceding.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong graciously approved the request by imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 子建漸分其父兄子弟外居郡戍，內外相顧，終獲保全。

translations.literal: Zijian gradually dispersed the fathers, elder and younger brothers, and sons of families to dwell outside at district garrisons; inside and outside watched over one another, and in the end preservation was achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Zijian gradually posted the fathers, brothers, and sons of local families to garrisons outside the city, so that those inside and out could keep watch on one another, and in this way the community was preserved.

sentences.zh: 及秦賊乘勝，屯營黑水，子建乃潛使掩襲，前後斬獲甚眾，威名赫然，先反者及此悉降。

translations.literal: When the Qin rebels seized victory and encamped at Black Water, Zijian then secretly sent men to launch a surprise attack; before and after many were beheaded and captured, his awesomeness was brilliant, and those who had first rebelled and those here all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qin rebels pressed their advantage and made camp at Black Water, Zijian sent troops in a secret raid. They killed and captured large numbers of enemy fighters, his prestige soared, and those who had rebelled earlier submitted one after another.

sentences.zh: 乃間使上聞，肅宗甚嘉之，詔子建兼尚書為行臺，刺史如故。

translations.literal: Then through an intermediary he reported upward; Suzong greatly praised this, and ordered Zijian additionally as Director of the Secretariat to serve as Mobile Office, regional inspector as before.
translations.idiomatic: He sent word through a special messenger. Emperor Suzong was greatly pleased and appointed Zijian Director of the Secretariat with authority as a mobile imperial commission, while retaining his post as provincial governor.

sentences.zh: 於是威震蜀土，其梁、巴、二益、兩秦之事，皆所節度。

translations.literal: Thereupon his prestige shook the lands of Shu; matters of Liang, Ba, the two Yis, and the two Qins were all under his coordination.
translations.idiomatic: His authority now extended across the Shu region, and he had supervisory power over affairs in Liang, Ba, the two Yizhou provinces, and the two Qin provinces.

sentences.zh: 梁州刺史傅豎眼子敬和中心以為愧，在洛大行貨賄，以圖行臺。

translations.literal: Fu Shuyan's son Jinghe, Regional Inspector of Liangzhou, felt shame at heart; in Luoyang he extensively engaged in bribery, seeking the mobile office position.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jinghe, son of Liangzhou governor Fu Shuyan, felt deeply aggrieved. In Luoyang he spent lavishly on bribes, angling for the mobile commission post.

sentences.zh: 先是，子建亦屢求歸京師，至此，乃遣刺史唐永代焉，[5]豎眼因為行臺。

translations.literal: Before this, Zijian also had repeatedly sought return to the capital; at this point, Regional Inspector Tang Yong was sent to replace him, [5] and Shuyan thereby became mobile office.
translations.idiomatic: Zijian had already been asking repeatedly to return to the capital. At this juncture Tang Yong was sent as provincial governor to replace him, [5] and Fu Shuyan took over the mobile commission.

sentences.zh: 子建將還，羣氐慕戀，相率斷道。

translations.literal: As Zijian was about to return, the Di tribes, cherishing attachment, one after another blocked the road.
translations.idiomatic: When Zijian prepared to leave, the Di people, who cherished him, gathered in groups and blocked the road.

sentences.zh: 主簿楊僧覆先行曉喻，諸氐忿曰：「我留刺史，爾送出也！」

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Yang Sengfu went ahead first to explain and persuade; the Di angrily said: "We kept the regional inspector—you are the ones to see him off!"
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk Yang Sengfu went ahead to reason with them. The Di shouted angrily: "We kept our governor here—you're the ones trying to escort him away!

sentences.zh: 斫之數創，幾死。

translations.literal: They hacked him with many wounds, and he nearly died.
translations.idiomatic: They hacked him repeatedly and nearly killed him.

sentences.zh: 子建徐加慰譬，旬日方得前行，吏人贈遺，一無所受。

translations.literal: Zijian gradually added consolation and instruction; only after ten days could he proceed forward; gifts from officials and people he accepted not one.
translations.idiomatic: Zijian gently soothed and reassured them, and only after ten days could he continue on his way. He accepted none of the gifts the officials and commoners pressed upon him.

sentences.zh: 而東益氐、蜀尋反，攻逼唐永，永棄城而走，乃喪一藩矣。

translations.literal: But the Di and Shu of Eastern Yizhou soon rebelled, pressing Tang Yong in attack; Yong abandoned the city and fled—thus a frontier defense was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Di and Shu peoples of Eastern Yizhou rebelled, attacked Tang Yong, and drove him to abandon the city and flee—the province was lost.

sentences.zh: 初永之走，子建客有沙門曇璨及鉅鹿人耿顯皆沒落氐手，及知子建之客，垂泣追衣物還之，送出白馬。

translations.literal: When Yong fled, among Zijian's retainers the monk Tancan and Julu native Geng Xian both fell into Di hands; when they learned they were Zijian's guests, weeping they pursued to return their clothing and goods, escorting them out at White Horse.
translations.idiomatic: When Yong fled, two of Zijian's companions—the monk Tancan and Geng Xian of Julu—were seized by the Di. Learning they were Zijian's men, the Di wept, restored their stolen possessions, and saw them safely out at White Horse Pass.

sentences.zh: 遺愛所被如此。

translations.literal: The legacy love he left was such as this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the depth of affection he had inspired.

sentences.zh: 自國家開華陽等郡，梁州邢巒、益州傅豎眼及子建為最。

translations.literal: Since the state opened Huayang and other commanderies, Xing Luan of Liangzhou, Fu Shuyan of Yizhou, and Zijian were foremost.
translations.idiomatic: From the time the empire established Huayang and other districts, Xing Luan in Liangzhou, Fu Shuyan in Yizhou, and Zijian were ranked the finest governors.

sentences.zh: 初，子建為前軍將軍，十年不徙，在洛閑暇，與吏部尚書李韶、韶從弟延寔頗為弈棊，時人謂為耽好。

translations.literal: Initially Zijian was General of the Vanguard; for ten years he was not transferred; in Luoyang in leisure, with Director of Personnel Li Shao and Shao's cousin Yanbao he fairly often played weiqi; people of the time called it a distracting passion.
translations.idiomatic: When Zijian served as General of the Vanguard he remained in that post for ten years without transfer. During his idle days in Luoyang he often played go with Li Shao, Director of Personnel, and Shao's cousin Yanbao—pastimes that contemporaries dismissed as frivolous indulgence.

sentences.zh: 子建每曰：「棊於機權廉勇之際，得之深矣。

translations.literal: Zijian often said: "In weiqi, at the junctures of stratagem, authority, integrity, and courage, one gains profound insight.
translations.idiomatic: Zijian often remarked: "In the game of go one learns deeply about timing, authority, integrity, and courage at decisive moments.

sentences.zh: 且吾未為時用，博弈可也。」

translations.literal: Moreover, I am not yet employed by the times—gaming and gambling are permissible."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, I have not yet been put to use by the age—a game or two is harmless enough."

sentences.zh: 及一臨邊事，凡經五年，未曾對局。

translations.literal: Once he took charge of border affairs, for fully five years he never faced a board.
translations.idiomatic: Once he took up frontier duties, he went five full years without playing a single match.

sentences.zh: 還洛後，俄拜常侍、衞尉卿。

translations.literal: After returning to Luoyang, he was soon appointed Regular Attendant and Commandant of Guards.
translations.idiomatic: After returning to Luoyang he was soon made Regular Attendant and Commandant of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 初，元顥內逼，莊帝北幸，子建謂所親盧義僖曰：「北海自絕社稷，稱藩蕭衍，吾老矣，豈能為陪臣？」

translations.literal: Initially, when Yuan Hao pressed inward, Emperor Zhuang fled north; Zijian said to his close associate Lu Yixi: "Beihai has severed himself from the state altars and declared himself vassal to Xiao Yan—I am old; how could I become a subordinate minister?"
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao advanced on the capital and Emperor Zhuang fled north, Zijian told his confidant Lu Yixi: "Beihai has abandoned the imperial altars and declared himself a vassal of Xiao Yan. I am too old to serve as anyone's subordinate minister.

sentences.zh: 遂攜家口居洛南，顥平乃歸。

translations.literal: Thereupon taking family and dependents he dwelt south of the Luo River; when Hao was pacified he then returned.
translations.idiomatic: He moved his family south of the Luo River, and only returned after Yuan Hao's defeat.

sentences.zh: 先苦風痺，及此遂甚，以卿任有務，屢上書乞身，特除右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Previously he suffered painful rheumatism; at this time it grew severe; because of his court duties, he repeatedly submitted memorials begging to retire; specially appointed Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He had long suffered from rheumatism, which now worsened considerably. Burdened by official responsibilities despite his illness, he repeatedly petitioned to retire and was specially appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness on the Right.

sentences.zh: 邢杲之平，太傅李延寔子侍中彧為大使，撫慰東土，時外戚貴盛，送客填門，子建亦往候別。

translations.literal: When Xing Gao was pacified, Grand Tutor Li Yanbao's son, Attendant-in-Ordinary Yu, was grand envoy to console the eastern lands; at that time the emperor's maternal relatives were noble and flourishing, farewell guests filled the gates, and Zijian also went to bid farewell.
translations.idiomatic: After the suppression of Xing Gao's rebellion, Li Yu—son of Grand Tutor Li Yanbao and Attendant-in-Ordinary—was sent as imperial envoy to pacify the eastern provinces. The emperor's powerful in-laws saw such envoys off in great numbers, and Zijian went to bid Yu farewell as well.

sentences.zh: 延寔曰：「小兒今行，何以相勗？」

translations.literal: Yanbao said: "My young son departs today—what counsel have you to offer?"
translations.idiomatic: Yanbao asked: "My son is setting out today—what advice would you give him?

sentences.zh: 子建曰：「益以盈滿為誡。」

translations.literal: Zijian said: "Admonish him that fullness and excess are to be taken as warning."
translations.idiomatic: Zijian replied: "Warn him against the dangers of excess and overreach."

sentences.zh: 延寔悵然久之。

translations.literal: Yanbao was long wistful and sorrowful.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbao stood in gloomy silence for a long while.

sentences.zh: 及莊帝殺尒朱榮，遇禍於河陰者其家率相弔賀。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang killed Erzhu Rong, families of those who met calamity at Heyin mostly congratulated one another in condolence.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Zhuang had Erzhu Rong killed, families whose relatives had been killed at Heyin exchanged ostensible condolences that were really celebrations.

sentences.zh: 太尉李虔第二子仁曜，子建之女壻，往亦見害。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Li Qian's second son Renyao, Zijian's son-in-law, also went and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Renyao, second son of Grand Commandant Li Qian and Zijian's son-in-law, was among the dead.

sentences.zh: 子建謂姨弟盧道虔曰：「朝廷誅翦權強，凶徒尚梗，未聞有奇謀異略，恐不可濟。

translations.literal: Zijian said to his cousin-in-law Lu Daoxian: "The court has executed and cut down the powerful; wicked ruffians still obstruct; I have not heard of any extraordinary schemes or different strategies—I fear success may be impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Zijian told his cousin Lu Daoxian: "The court has struck down a powerful faction, but dangerous men still hold out, and I hear nothing of any bold strategy. I doubt this will end well.

sentences.zh: 此乃李門禍始，弔賀無乃怱怱？」

translations.literal: This is the beginning of disaster for the Li clan—is congratulatory condolence not too hasty?
translations.idiomatic: This looks like the start of calamity for the Li family. Surely their celebrations are premature?

sentences.zh: 及永安之後，李氏宗族流離，或遇誅夷，如其所慮。

translations.literal: After the Yong'an era, the Li clan was scattered and displaced, some meeting execution and extermination, as he had foreseen.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yong'an period the Li clan was uprooted and destroyed, just as he had predicted.

sentences.zh: 後歷左光祿大夫，加散騎常侍、驃騎大將軍。

translations.literal: Later he served as Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, additionally Grand Master for Gentlemen of the Palace and General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and was further appointed Gentleman-in-Attendant and General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 子建自出為藩牧，董司山南，居脂膏之中，遇天下多事，正身潔己，不以財利經懷。

translations.literal: From the time Zijian went out as frontier governor, overseeing the south of the mountains, dwelling in rich lands, encountering a world of many troubles, he rectified himself and purified his person, not letting wealth and profit enter his thoughts.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Zijian took office as a regional governor overseeing the southern mountains—a post rich in opportunity, in turbulent times—he kept himself upright and never let greed touch his mind.

sentences.zh: 及歸京師，家人衣食常不周贍，清素之迹，著於終始。

translations.literal: When he returned to the capital, his family's food and clothing were constantly insufficient; his record of purity and simplicity was evident from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: Even after returning to the capital his family often lacked for necessities. His reputation for plain, honest living never wavered.

sentences.zh: 性存重慎，不雜交遊，唯與尚書盧義僖、姨弟涇州刺史盧道裕雅相親昵。

translations.literal: His nature held weight and caution; he did not mingle in miscellaneous socializing, only with Director Lu Yixi and his cousin Regional Inspector of Jingzhou Lu Daoyu was he elegantly close and intimate.
translations.idiomatic: He was cautious by nature and kept his social circle small. Only Director of the Secretariat Lu Yixi and his cousin Lu Daoyu, governor of Jingzhou, counted as close friends.

sentences.zh: 及疾篤，顧敕二子曰：「死生大分，含氣所同，世有厚葬，吾平生不取，籧篨裸身，又非吾意。

translations.literal: When his illness was grave, he turned and admonished his two sons: "Life and death are a great allotment, shared by all who breathe; the world has lavish burial—I throughout life have not taken to it; coarse mat and naked body is again not my intent.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he instructed his two sons: "Life and death are fate's great division, shared by every living being. Lavish funerals are common, but I have never approved of them—and burial on a straw mat with an unclothed body is not my wish either.

sentences.zh: 氣絕之後，斂以時服。

translations.literal: After breath ceases, dress me in the garments of the season for encoffining.
translations.idiomatic: After I die, dress my body in my ordinary clothes.

sentences.zh: 吾生年契闊，[6]前後三娶，合葬之事，抑又非古。

translations.literal: My years of life have been long and parted, [6] with three marriages before and after; joint burial again is not ancient custom.
translations.idiomatic: My life has been long and marked by separations, [6] and I married three times. Joint burial with all my wives is not the old way.

sentences.zh: 且汝二母先在舊塋，墳地久固，已有定別。

translations.literal: Moreover, your two mothers are already in the old tomb enclosure; the grave land has long been settled, with fixed distinctions already made.
translations.idiomatic: Your two mothers already lie in the old family cemetery, where their graves were assigned long ago.

sentences.zh: 唯汝次母墓在外耳，可遷入兆域，依班而定，行於吾墓之後。

translations.literal: Only your stepmother's grave is outside; she may be moved into the burial precinct, placed according to rank, positioned behind my tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Only your stepmother's grave lies elsewhere. Move it into the family plot, assign her place according to seniority, and lay her out behind my tomb.

sentences.zh: 如此足矣，不須祔合。

translations.literal: This suffices; there is no need for attachment in joint burial.
translations.idiomatic: That will be enough—there is no need to bury us all together in one grave.

sentences.zh: 當順吾心，勿令吾有遺恨。」

translations.literal: You must accord with my heart; do not let me have remaining regret.
translations.idiomatic: Do as I wish, so that I may die without regret.

sentences.zh: 永熙二年春，卒于洛陽孝義里舍，時年六十三，贈儀同三司、定州刺史，諡曰文靜。

translations.literal: In spring of the second year of Yongxi he died at his residence in Xiaoyi Lane, Luoyang, aged sixty-three; posthumously given Chief Grand Officer of State and Regional Inspector of Dingzhou, posthumous title Wenjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Yongxi 2 he died at his home in Xiaoyi Lane, Luoyang, at the age of sixty-three. He was posthumously honored as Chief Minister of State with Equal Standing and governor of Dingzhou, and given the posthumous name Wenjing.

sentences.zh: 二子，收、祚。

translations.literal: Two sons: Shou and Zuo.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Shou and Zuo.

sentences.zh: 收字伯起，小字佛助。

translations.literal: Shou, courtesy name Boqi, childhood name Fozhu.
translations.idiomatic: Shou, styled Boqi, childhood name Fozhu.

sentences.zh: 年十五，頗已屬文。

translations.literal: At age fifteen, he could already compose literary pieces.
translations.idiomatic: By fifteen he was already writing capably.

sentences.zh: 及隨父赴邊，值四方多難，好習騎射，欲以武藝自達。

translations.literal: When he followed his father to the frontier, encountering many difficulties in all quarters, he loved to practice riding and archery, wishing to advance through martial arts.
translations.idiomatic: When he accompanied his father to the frontier during widespread turmoil, he took up riding and archery, hoping to make his way through military skill.

sentences.zh: 滎陽鄭伯調之曰：「魏郎弄戟多少？」

translations.literal: Zheng Bo of Xingyang teased him: "Young Wei, how much do you know about wielding a halberd?"
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Bo of Xingyang mocked him: "Young Wei, how much do you really know about handling a spear?

sentences.zh: 收慚，遂折節讀書。

translations.literal: Shou was ashamed, and thereupon reined in his will to read books.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply embarrassed, Shou turned to serious study.

sentences.zh: 夏月坐板牀，隨樹陰諷誦，積年，牀板為之銳減，而精力不輟。

translations.literal: In summer months sitting on a plank bed, following the tree shade to recite and chant, over accumulated years the bed planks were sharply worn down by this, yet his vigor did not slacken.
translations.idiomatic: In summer he sat on a wooden couch in the shifting shade of a tree, reciting his texts. Year after year he wore the boards thin, yet his dedication never flagged.

sentences.zh: 以文華顯。

translations.literal: Through literary brilliance he became distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to prominence through his literary talent.

sentences.zh: 初以父功除太學博士，及尒朱榮於河陰濫害朝士，收亦在圍中，以日晏獲免。

translations.literal: Initially through his father's merit he was appointed Erudite of the Imperial Academy; when Erzhu Rong at Heyin indiscriminately slaughtered court officials, Shou was also within the encirclement, and because the day was late he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: He first received appointment as Erudite of the Imperial Academy through his father's service. When Erzhu Rong massacred court officials at Heyin, Shou was caught in the roundup but spared because nightfall had come.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書李神儁重收才學，奏授司徒記室參軍。

translations.literal: Director of Personnel Li Shenjun valued Shou's talent and learning, memorialized to grant him Secretary in the Office of the Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shenjun, Director of Personnel, admired Shou's talents and recommended him for appointment as secretary in the Office of the Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 永安三年，除北主客郎中。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yong'an, appointed Chief of the Northern Bureau of Receiving Guests.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongan 3 he was appointed chief of the northern office for receiving foreign guests.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝立，妙簡近侍，詔試收為封禪書，收下筆便就，不立草稿，文將千言，所改無幾。

translations.literal: When the Former Deposed Emperor ascended, finely selecting close attendants, he ordered Shou tested with a fengshan document; Shou took brush and immediately completed it, not drafting preliminary notes—the text nearly a thousand words, with scarcely any revisions.
translations.idiomatic: When the former deposed emperor took the throne, he selected close attendants carefully and tested Shou by ordering him to compose a fengshan proclamation. Shou wrote it straight off without a draft—nearly a thousand characters, with hardly a correction.

sentences.zh: 時黃門郎賈思同侍立，深奇之。

translations.literal: At that time Attendant of the Yellow Gates Jia Sitong stood attending and was deeply amazed.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant of the Yellow Gates Jia Sitong, standing nearby, was deeply impressed.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：[7]「雖七步之才，無以過此。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: [7]"Even talent for seven paces could not surpass this."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor remarked: [7]"Not even Cao Zhi's seven-pace talent could surpass this.

sentences.zh: 遷散騎侍郎，尋敕典起居注，并修國史。

translations.literal: Promoted to Gentleman Attendant-in-Ordinary, soon ordered to take charge of the Daily Records and also compile the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Gentleman Attendant-in-Ordinary and soon put in charge of the imperial diary while also compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 俄兼中書侍郎，年二十六。

translations.literal: Soon additionally Vice Director of the Secretariat, age twenty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was also named Vice Director of the Secretariat—at only twenty-six.

sentences.zh: 出帝初，又詔收攝本職，文誥填積，事咸稱旨。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Departure Emperor's reign, again ordered Shou to resume his original post; documents and decrees piled up, and affairs all matched his intent.
translations.idiomatic: When the Departure Emperor came to the throne, Shou was recalled to his former duties. Official documents piled up, and everything he wrote met with approval.

sentences.zh: 黃門郎崔㥄從齊獻武王入朝，熏灼於世，收初不詣門。

translations.literal: Attendant of the Yellow Gates Cui Lin followed Duke Xianwu of Qi into court, blazing hot in the world; Shou at first did not visit his door.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Lin, Attendant of the Yellow Gates, rode into court in the train of Duke Xianwu of Qi and wielded enormous influence. Shou never went near his gate.

sentences.zh: 㥄為帝登祚赦，云「朕託體孝文」，收嗤其率直。

translations.literal: Lin composed the amnesty for the emperor's accession, saying "I take my body from Emperor Xiaowen"; Shou scoffed at its bluntness.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin drafted the emperor's accession amnesty with the phrase "I take my form from Emperor Xiaowen," Shou laughed at its blunt literalism.

sentences.zh: 正員郎李慎以告之，㥄深忿忌。

translations.literal: Regular Gentleman Li Shen told him of this; Lin deeply resented and bore jealousy.
translations.idiomatic: Regular Gentleman Li Shen reported Shou's mockery, and Lin nursed a deep grudge.

sentences.zh: 時前廢帝殂，令收為詔，㥄乃宣言：「收普泰世出入幃幄，一日造詔，優為詞旨，然則義旗之士，盡為逆人；

translations.literal: At that time when the Former Deposed Emperor died, Shou was ordered to draft the edict; Lin then proclaimed: "Shou during the Putai era went in and out of the curtain chambers; in one day he drafted an edict with words finely tuned—in that case the men who raised the righteous banners are all made rebels;
translations.idiomatic: When the former deposed emperor died and Shou was ordered to draft the mourning edict, Lin publicly accused him: "During the Putai reign Shou moved freely in the inner court. He can turn out a polished edict in a day—so by that logic every man who raised the righteous banner becomes a rebel.

sentences.zh: 又收父老合解官歸侍。」

translations.literal: Moreover, Shou's father is old and ought properly to resign office and return home to attend him."
translations.idiomatic: And Shou's elderly father should by rights resign and return home so his son can care for him.

sentences.zh: 南臺將加彈劾，賴尚書辛雄為言於中尉綦儁，乃解。

translations.literal: The Southern Censorate was about to impeach; thanks to Director Xin Xiong speaking on his behalf to Chief Commandant Qi Jun, the matter was resolved.
translations.idiomatic: The southern censorate prepared to impeach him, but Director Xin Xiong interceded with Chief Commandant Qi Jun, and the case was dropped.

sentences.zh: 收有賤生弟仲同先未齒錄，因此怖懼，上籍，遣還鄉扶侍。

translations.literal: Shou had a younger half-brother Zhongtong who had not before been entered in the register; from this fear he submitted his name to the register and sent him home to the village to attend and support.
translations.idiomatic: Shou had a younger half-brother, Zhongtong, who had never been officially registered. Frightened by Lin's attack, Shou entered him in the family register and sent him home to care for their father.

sentences.zh: 出帝嘗大發士卒，狩於嵩少之南，旬有六日，時既寒苦，朝野嗟怨。

translations.literal: The Departure Emperor once greatly mobilized troops and hunted south of Song and Shao for sixteen days; the season was already bitter cold, and court and countryside lamented in complaint.
translations.idiomatic: The Departure Emperor once mobilized a large force and hunted south of Mount Song for sixteen days. The weather was bitterly cold, and people throughout the court and countryside complained bitterly.

sentences.zh: 帝與從官皆胡服而騎，宮人及諸妃主雜其間，奇伎異飾，多非禮度。

translations.literal: The emperor and attendant officials all wore nomadic dress and rode; palace women and various consorts and princesses were mixed among them; strange skills and exotic adornments mostly departed from ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and his attendants rode in nomadic dress, with palace women and imperial consorts mingled among them, performing outlandish stunts and wearing bizarre costumes—most of it well outside proper ceremonial bounds.

sentences.zh: 收欲言則畏懼，欲默不能已，乃上南狩賦以諷焉，年二十七，雖富言淫麗，而終歸雅正。

translations.literal: Shou wished to speak yet feared; wished to be silent yet could not stop himself, and so submitted an "Ode on the Southern Hunt" to admonish thereby; age twenty-seven—though the words were rich and luxuriant, in the end they returned to the elegant and upright.
translations.idiomatic: Shou wanted to speak out but feared retribution, yet could not keep silent. At twenty-seven he submitted his "Rhapsody on the Southern Hunt" as a veiled remonstrance. Though lushly ornate, it ultimately upheld moral propriety.

sentences.zh: 帝手詔報焉，甚見褒美。

translations.literal: The emperor personally wrote an edict in reply, greatly praising and commending it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor responded with a handwritten note lavishing praise on the piece.

sentences.zh: 鄭伯謂曰：「卿不遇老夫，猶應逐兔。」

translations.literal: Zheng Bo said to him: "Had you not met this old man, you would still be chasing rabbits."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Bo told him: "If you had never met me, you'd still be out hunting rabbits.

sentences.zh: 初，齊獻武王固讓天柱大將軍，帝敕收為詔，令遂所請，欲加相國，問收相國品秩，收以實對，帝遂止。

translations.literal: Initially, Duke Xianwu of Qi firmly declined the title General of the Heavenly Pillar; the emperor ordered Shou to draft the edict, directing acceptance of his request; wishing to add the title Chancellor of State, he asked Shou about the rank and grade of Chancellor; Shou answered according to fact, and the emperor thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke Xianwu of Qi steadfastly declined the title General of the Heavenly Pillar, the emperor had Shou draft the edict granting his wish. The emperor then considered adding the title Chancellor of State, asked Shou about its rank in the official hierarchy, and when Shou answered honestly, abandoned the idea.

sentences.zh: 收既未測主相之意，以前事不安，求解，詔許焉。

translations.literal: Shou had not yet fathomed the lord and chancellor's intent; uneasy over earlier affairs, he sought release; an edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to read the intentions of the emperor and the duke, and unsettled by earlier troubles, Shou asked to resign—and was allowed to do so.

sentences.zh: 久之，除帝兄子廣平王贊開府從事中郎，收不敢辭，乃為庭竹賦以致己意。

translations.literal: After some time, appointed Attendant of the Staff for the Prince of Guangping, the emperor's brother's son Zan, with an open office; Shou dared not decline, and so composed an "Ode on the Bamboo in the Courtyard" to convey his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Some time later he was appointed attendant in the prince of Guangping's household—the prince was the emperor's nephew. Shou could not refuse, but wrote his "Rhapsody on the Court Bamboo" to express his true feelings.

sentences.zh: 尋兼中書舍人，與濟陰溫子昇、河間邢子才齊譽，世號三才。

translations.literal: Soon additionally Secretariat Aide; together with Wen Zisheng of Jiyin and Xing Zicai of Hejian equally renowned—the age called them the Three Talents.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became a secretariat aide and, together with Wen Zisheng of Jiyin and Xing Zicai of Hejian, earned equal renown as the Three Talents of the age.

sentences.zh: 時出帝猜忌獻武，內有間隙，收遂以疾固辭而免。

translations.literal: At that time the Departure Emperor suspected Xianwu; internally there were rifts; Shou thereupon pleaded illness, firmly declined, and was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Departure Emperor grew suspicious of Xianwu and court factions split, Shou pleaded illness and managed to get himself relieved of duty.

sentences.zh: 其舅崔孝芬怪而問之，收曰：「懼有晉陽之甲。」

translations.literal: His uncle Cui Xiaofen, puzzled, asked him; Shou said: "I fear there will be armor from Jinyang."
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Cui Xiaofen asked why. Shou answered: "I fear troops will march from Jinyang."

sentences.zh: 尋而獻武南上，帝西入關。

translations.literal: Soon after Xianwu marched south, the emperor entered the Pass to the west.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xianwu advanced south and the emperor fled west into the pass.

sentences.zh: 收兼通直散騎常侍副王昕聘蕭衍，昕風流文辯，收辭藻富逸，衍及其羣臣咸加敬異。

translations.literal: Shou additionally served as Direct Attendant-in-Ordinary and Deputy to Wang Xin on an embassy to Xiao Yan; Xin was refined in manner and eloquent in argument, Shou's diction rich and unrestrained; Yan and all his ministers greatly showed respect and wonder.
translations.idiomatic: Shou served as envoy deputy to Wang Xin on a mission to Xiao Yan. Xin was polished and articulate; Shou's prose was rich and fluent. Yan and his entire court treated them with marked respect.

sentences.zh: 先是，南北初和，李諧、盧元明首通使命，二人才器，並為鄰國所重。

translations.literal: Before this, when north and south first made peace, Li Xie and Lu Yuanming first carried missions; the two men's talents and capacity were both held in esteem by the neighboring state.
translations.idiomatic: When north and south first made peace, Li Xie and Lu Yuanming were the pioneering envoys, and both were held in high regard across the border.

sentences.zh: 至此，衍稱曰：「盧、李命世，王、魏中興，未知後來復何如耳？」

translations.literal: At this point Yan declared: "Lu and Li were men of their age; Wang and Wei revive the tradition—who knows what those to come will be like?"
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion Yan said: "Lu and Li were geniuses of their generation; Wang and Wei renew that glory—but who knows whether those who follow will measure up?

sentences.zh: 文襄啟收兼散騎常侍，修國史。

translations.literal: Wen Xiang memorialized Shou as additionally Attendant-in-Ordinary, compiling national history.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Xiang recommended Shou for appointment as Attendant-in-Ordinary with responsibility for compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 武定二年，除正常侍，領兼中書侍郎，仍修史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wuding, appointed Regular Attendant, concurrently leading and additionally as Vice Director of the Secretariat, still compiling history.
translations.idiomatic: In Wuding 2 he was appointed Regular Attendant and concurrently Vice Director of the Secretariat, continuing his work on the histories.

sentences.zh: 帝宴百僚，問何故名人日，皆莫能知。

translations.literal: The emperor feasted the hundred officials and asked why the day is called Human Day; none could know.
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet for the hundred officials the emperor asked why the seventh day of the New Year was called Human Day. No one knew.

sentences.zh: 收對曰：「晉議郎董勛答問，稱俗云正月一日為鷄，二日為狗，三日為猪，四日為羊，五日為牛，六日為馬，七日為人。

translations.literal: Shou answered: "Jin Discussion Officer Dong Xun in reply to questions said the common saying is: first day of first month is the cock, second day the dog, third the pig, fourth the sheep, fifth the ox, sixth the horse, seventh the person.
translations.idiomatic: Shou answered: "According to Dong Xun, Discussion Officer of the Jin dynasty, folk tradition holds that the first day of the first month is the day of the rooster, the second the dog, the third the pig, the fourth the sheep, the fifth the ox, the sixth the horse, and the seventh the day of humanity.

sentences.zh: 時邢卲亦在側，甚恧焉。

translations.literal: At that time Xing Shao was also at the side, and was greatly ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Shao, standing nearby, flushed with embarrassment.

sentences.zh: 自南北和好，書下紙每云「想彼境內寧靜，此率土安和」。

translations.literal: Since north and south made peace, every letter sent down on paper always said, "We trust that within your borders all is tranquil, and here throughout the land all is at peace."
translations.idiomatic: After the northern and southern courts made peace, their diplomatic letters routinely opened with the phrase: "We trust your realm is at peace, and all is well throughout our land."

sentences.zh: 蕭衍後使，其書乃去「彼」字，自稱猶著「此」，欲示無外之意。

translations.literal: Later envoys from Xiao Yan removed the character "your" from their letters, while still using "our" for themselves, wishing to show the meaning of having no outside realm.
translations.idiomatic: Later, envoys from Xiao Yan dropped the word "your" from their letters while still using "our," intending to imply that no foreign realm existed beyond their own.

sentences.zh: 收定報書云：「想境內清晏，今萬國安和。」

translations.literal: Shou fixed the reply letter to say: "We trust the realm is clear and tranquil; now the myriad states are at peace."
translations.idiomatic: Shou drafted the reply to read: "We trust the realm is peaceful; now all nations under heaven enjoy harmony."

sentences.zh: 南人復書，依以為體。

translations.literal: The southerners in their reply letters followed this as the standard form.
translations.idiomatic: The southern court adopted this phrasing as the standard in their return correspondence.

sentences.zh: 後獻武入朝，靜帝授相國，固讓，令收為啟。

translations.literal: Later when Xianwu entered court, Emperor Jingdi invested him as Chancellor of State; he firmly declined, and ordered Shou to draft the memorial of refusal.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianwu later came to court, Emperor Jing invested him as Chancellor of State. He steadfastly declined, and had Shou draft the memorial of refusal.

sentences.zh: 啟成呈上，文襄時侍側，獻武指收曰：「此人當復為崔光。」

translations.literal: When the memorial was completed and presented, Wen Xiang was attending at the side; Xianwu pointed to Shou and said: "This man will again become another Cui Guang."
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was finished and submitted, Wen Xiang stood nearby. Xianwu pointed at Shou and said: "This man will become another Cui Guang."

sentences.zh: 四年，獻武於西門豹祠宴集，謂司馬子如曰：「魏收為史官，書吾善惡。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Xianwu held a banquet at the Shrine of Ximen Bao and said to Sima Ziru: "Wei Shou as historiographer writes my good and ill.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Xianwu hosted a banquet at the Shrine of Ximen Bao and said to Sima Ziru: "Wei Shou, as historiographer, will record my virtues and faults.

sentences.zh: 聞北伐時，諸貴常餉史官飲食，司馬僕射頗曾餉不？」

translations.literal: I hear that during the northern campaign the nobles often supplied food and drink to the historiographers—Vice Director Sima, did you ever supply any?"
translations.idiomatic: I hear that during the northern campaign the nobles often treated the historiographers to meals—Vice Director Sima, did you ever send any gifts?

sentences.zh: 因共大笑。

translations.literal: Thereupon they all laughed heartily together.
translations.idiomatic: They all burst out laughing together.

sentences.zh: 仍謂收曰：「卿勿見元康等在吾目下趨走，謂吾以為勤勞，我後世身名在卿手，勿謂我不知。」

translations.literal: He then said to Shou: "Do not see Yuan Kang and the rest bustling before my eyes and think I consider it labor; my posthumous name and reputation are in your hands—do not suppose I am unaware."
translations.idiomatic: Then he told Shou: "Do not see Yuan Kang and the others scurrying about before me and think I mistake it for true diligence. My legacy rests in your hands—do not imagine I do not know it."

sentences.zh: 尋加兼著作郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Shou was soon additionally appointed Compiler.

sentences.zh: 靜帝曾季秋大射，普令賦詩，收詩末云：「尺書徵建鄴，折簡召長安。」

translations.literal: Emperor Jing once held a grand autumn archery ceremony and universally ordered poems composed; the closing lines of Shou's poem read: "A written summons will summon Jiankang; a folded letter will summon Chang'an."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing once held a grand autumn archery ceremony and ordered all officials to compose poems. Shou's poem ended with the lines: "A written summons will summon Jiankang; a folded letter will summon Chang'an."

sentences.zh: 文襄壯之，顧謂人曰：「在朝今有魏收，便是國之光采。

translations.literal: Wen Xiang was impressed and, turning to those present, said: "In court today there is Wei Shou—that itself is the nation's glory.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Xiang was impressed and said to those present: "With Wei Shou in court today, the state itself shines brighter.

sentences.zh: 雅俗文墨，通達縱橫，我亦使子才、子昇時有所作，至於詞氣並不及之。

translations.literal: In refined and common letters, in prose and policy, he is thoroughly versed and resourceful; I also have Zicai and Zisheng compose pieces from time to time, yet in tone and spirit they cannot match him.
translations.idiomatic: Whether in refined or plain writing, in prose or statecraft, he is masterful and versatile. I have Zicai and Zisheng write on occasion, but neither matches his force of expression.

sentences.zh: 吾或意有所懷，忘而不語，語而不盡，意有未及。

translations.literal: Sometimes I have thoughts I hold and forget to speak, or speak yet do not fully express, or have intentions not yet reached.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes I have thoughts I keep to myself, or words I leave unfinished, or ideas I have not yet fully formed.

sentences.zh: 及收呈草，皆以周悉。

translations.literal: When Shou presented his draft, all were complete and thorough.
translations.idiomatic: When Shou submitted his drafts, they captured everything completely.

sentences.zh: 此亦難有。」

translations.literal: This too is hard to match."
translations.idiomatic: That kind of talent is rare indeed.

sentences.zh: 又敕兼主客郎，接蕭衍使謝珽徐陵。

translations.literal: He also ordered Shou additionally to serve as Chief of Receiving Guests, receiving the envoys of Xiao Yan, Xie Yan and Xu Ling.
translations.idiomatic: He also appointed Shou chief of receiving guests to host the envoys from Xiao Yan, Xie Yan and Xu Ling.

sentences.zh: 侯景既陷臺城，衍鄱陽王範時為合州刺史，文襄敕收以書喻之。

translations.literal: After Hou Jing had taken Taicheng, Fan, Prince of Poyang under Xiao Yan, was then Regional Inspector of Hezhou; Wen Xiang ordered Shou to write a letter to persuade him.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jing captured Taicheng, Fan, Prince of Poyang under Xiao Yan, was serving as governor of Hezhou. Wen Xiang ordered Shou to write a letter urging him to defect.

sentences.zh: 範得書，乃率部伍西上，□州刺史崔聖念入據其城。

translations.literal: Fan received the letter and thereupon led his troops westward; Regional Inspector Cui Shengian of □zhou entered and occupied his city.
translations.idiomatic: Fan received the letter and marched west with his troops, whereupon Governor Cui Shengian of □ Province entered and seized his city.

sentences.zh: 文襄謂收曰：「今定一州，卿有其力，猶恨『尺書徵建鄴』未效耳。」

translations.literal: Wen Xiang said to Shou: "Now one province is secured—you had a hand in it; I still regret that 'A written summons will summon Jiankang' has not yet taken effect."
translations.idiomatic: Wen Xiang told Shou: "We have secured a province today, and you played a part—but I still regret that your line about summoning Jiankang with a letter has not yet come true."

sentences.zh: 二年，受詔撰魏史，除魏尹，故優以祿力，專在史閣，不知郡事。

translations.literal: In the second year, he received an edict to compile the History of Wei, was appointed Administrator of Wei Capital, and therefore given generous salary and support, devoted entirely to the historiography office, unaware of commandery affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he received an edict to compile the History of Wei and was appointed administrator of the Wei capital. Given generous salary and support, he worked exclusively in the historiography office and paid no attention to local administration.

sentences.zh: 初，帝令羣臣各言志，收曰：「臣願得直筆東觀，早出魏書。」

translations.literal: Initially the emperor ordered the ministers each to state their ambitions; Shou said: "Your servant wishes to wield the straight brush at the Eastern Pavilion and bring forth the History of Wei early."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor first asked his ministers to declare their ambitions, Shou said: "I wish to write history with an honest brush at the Eastern Pavilion and complete the History of Wei without delay."

sentences.zh: 故帝使收專其任。

translations.literal: Therefore the emperor had Shou take sole charge of the task.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor therefore entrusted the entire project to Shou.

sentences.zh: 又詔平原王高隆之總監之，隆之署名而已。

translations.literal: An edict also appointed Prince of Pingyuan Gao Longzhi as general supervisor; Longzhi merely affixed his signature.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also named Prince of Pingyuan Gao Longzhi as general supervisor, but Longzhi did nothing more than sign his name.

sentences.zh: 帝敕收曰：「好直筆，我終不作魏太武誅史官。」

translations.literal: The emperor admonished Shou: "Write with a straight brush—I will never do as Emperor Taiwu of Wei and execute historiographers."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Shou: "Write honestly—I will never do as Emperor Taiwu of Wei did and kill the historiographers."

sentences.zh: 始魏初鄧淵撰代記十餘卷，其後崔浩典史，游雅、高允、程駿、李彪、崔光、李琰之世修其業。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wei, Deng Yuan compiled the Annals of the Dynasty in more than ten scrolls; thereafter Cui Hao took charge of the histories, and You Ya, Gao Yun, Cheng Jun, Li Biao, Cui Guang, and Li Yanzhi successively continued the work.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Wei, Deng Yuan compiled the Annals of the Dynasty in more than ten scrolls. Later Cui Hao directed the historiography, and You Ya, Gao Yun, Cheng Jun, Li Biao, Cui Guang, and Li Yanzhi carried on the tradition through successive generations.

sentences.zh: 浩為編年體，彪始分作紀表志傳，書猶未出。

translations.literal: Hao used the annalistic form; Biao first divided the work into annals, tables, treatises, and biographies, but the book had still not been published.
translations.idiomatic: Hao wrote in annalistic form; Biao first organized the work into annals, tables, treatises, and biographies, but the history had still not been published.

sentences.zh: 世宗時，命邢巒追撰高祖起居注，書至太和十四年，又命崔鴻、王遵業補續焉。

translations.literal: In Emperor Shizong's time, Xing Luan was ordered to compile the Daily Records of Emperor Gaozu, the text reaching to the fourteenth year of Taihe; Cui Hong and Wang Zunye were also ordered to continue it.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Shizong's reign Xing Luan was ordered to compile the Daily Records of Emperor Gaozu, bringing the account down to the fourteenth year of Taihe; Cui Hong and Wang Zunye were also ordered to continue the work.

sentences.zh: 下訖肅宗，事甚委悉。

translations.literal: It extended down to Emperor Suzong, and the events were very detailed.
translations.idiomatic: The record extended through Emperor Suzong and was exceedingly detailed.

sentences.zh: 濟陰王暉業撰辨宗室錄三十卷。

translations.literal: Prince of Jiyin Huiye compiled the Record of the Imperial Clan in thirty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jiyin Huiye compiled the Record of the Imperial Clan in thirty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 收於是與通直常侍房延祐，司空司馬辛元植，國子博士刁柔、裴昂之，尚書郎高孝幹博總斟酌，[8]以成魏書。

translations.literal: Shou thereupon, together with Direct Attendant Fang Yanyou, Secretary to the Minister of Works Xin Yuanzhi, Erudites Diao Rou and Pei Angzhi, and Gentleman of the Secretariat Gao Xiaogan, broadly gathered and weighed materials, [8] to complete the History of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Shou then worked with Direct Attendant Fang Yanyou, Secretary to the Minister of Works Xin Yuanzhi, Erudites Diao Rou and Pei Angzhi, and Gentleman of the Secretariat Gao Xiaogan to gather and evaluate sources broadly, [8] and complete the History of Wei.

sentences.zh: 辨定名稱，隨條甄舉，又搜採亡遺，綴續後事，備一代史籍，表而上聞。

translations.literal: He fixed names and titles, selected entries according to each category, also searched out what was lost and missing, patched and continued later events, completing the historical records of an entire dynasty, and submitted the tables in memorial to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He standardized names and titles, selected material category by category, recovered lost records, and continued the account of later events, completing the historical record of an entire dynasty, which he submitted to the throne.

sentences.zh: 勒成一代大典，凡十二紀、九十二列傳，合一百一十卷，五年三月奏上之。

translations.literal: He carved out the great canon of a generation: twelve annals and ninety-two biographical accounts in all, totaling one hundred and ten scrolls, memorialized and submitted in the third month of the fifth year.
translations.idiomatic: He produced the great historical canon of an age: twelve annals and ninety-two biographies, one hundred and ten scrolls in all, submitted in the third month of the fifth year.

sentences.zh: 秋，除梁州刺史，收以志未成，奏請終業，許之。

translations.literal: In autumn he was appointed Regional Inspector of Liangzhou; Shou, because the treatises were not yet complete, memorialized requesting to finish the work, and permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he was appointed governor of Liangzhou, but Shou petitioned to remain until the treatises were finished, and his request was granted.

sentences.zh: 十一月，復奏十志：天象四卷，地形三卷，律歷二卷，禮、樂四卷，食貨一卷，刑罰一卷，靈徵二卷，官氏二卷，釋老一卷，凡二十卷，續於紀傳，合一百三十卷，分為十二帙。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he again memorialized the ten treatises: Celestial Phenomena, four scrolls; Geography, three scrolls; Calendars and Chronology, two scrolls; Rites and Music, four scrolls; Food and Goods, one scroll; Punishments, one scroll; Spiritual Signs, two scrolls; Offices and Clans, two scrolls; Buddhism and Daoism, one scroll—twenty scrolls in all, continuing the annals and biographies, one hundred and thirty scrolls in total, divided into twelve fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he submitted the ten treatises: Celestial Phenomena (4 scrolls), Geography (3), Calendars and Chronology (2), Rites and Music (4), Food and Goods (1), Punishments (1), Spiritual Signs (2), Offices and Clans (2), and Buddhism and Daoism (1)—twenty scrolls in all, appended to the annals and biographies for a total of one hundred and thirty scrolls in twelve fascicles.

sentences.zh: 其史三十五例，二十五序，九十四論，前後二表一啟焉。

translations.literal: The history included thirty-five precedents, twenty-five prefaces, ninety-four disquisitions, and in all two tables and one memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The history also included thirty-five precedents, twenty-five prefaces, ninety-four disquisitions, and two tables plus one memorial.

sentences.zh: 魏書卷一百四 諸本此卷目錄注「闕」。

translations.literal: In all editions of the History of Wei, scroll 104, the table of contents notes "deficient."
translations.idiomatic: In every edition of the History of Wei, the table of contents for scroll 104 is marked "missing."

sentences.zh: 按卷後諸本皆無宋人校語，當是脫去。

translations.literal: According to examination, all editions after the scroll lack Song-dynasty collation notes; these must have been lost.
translations.idiomatic: Examination shows that no edition retains Song-dynasty collation notes after this scroll; they must have been lost.

sentences.zh: 此序刪節北史卷五六魏收傳，兼採他書，故也有溢出北史字句。

translations.literal: This preface is an abridgment of the biography of Wei Shou in scroll 56 of the History of the Northern Dynasties, with material also drawn from other books; hence there are passages that exceed the text of the Northern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: This preface is an abridgment of Wei Shou's biography in scroll 56 of the History of the Northern Dynasties, supplemented from other sources, which explains why some passages go beyond the Northern Dynasties text.

sentences.zh: 成帝世位終鉅鹿太守 錢氏考異卷二八云：「此成帝謂漢成帝也。

translations.literal: "In the reign of Emperor Cheng he ended as Administrator of Julu"—Qian's Textual Variants, scroll 28, says: "This Emperor Cheng refers to Emperor Cheng of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Regarding "In the reign of Emperor Cheng he ended as Administrator of Julu"—Qian's Textual Variants, scroll 28, states: "This Emperor Cheng refers to Emperor Cheng of Han.

sentences.zh: 魏歆仕於漢成帝朝，而其子悅乃仕於元魏太武之世，此理之所必無者。

translations.literal: Wei Xin served in the court of Emperor Cheng of Han, yet his son Yue served in the era of Emperor Taiwu of Northern Wei—this is something reason absolutely cannot allow.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xin served under Emperor Cheng of Han, yet his son Yue served under Emperor Taiwu of Northern Wei—something that reason flatly cannot accept.

sentences.zh: 伯起亦通人，何至憒憒乃爾。

translations.literal: Boqi too was a man of broad learning—how could he have been so muddled as this?
translations.idiomatic: Boqi was himself a learned man—how could he have been so confused?

sentences.zh: 良由魏史自序久亡，後人節取北史補之，而北史又有脫簡，後人無從校正爾。」

translations.literal: Surely because Wei Shou's original authorial preface to the History of Wei had long been lost, later men excerpted the Northern Dynasties to fill the gap, and the Northern Dynasties itself had lacunae that later men had no means to correct."
translations.idiomatic: The explanation is surely that Wei Shou's original authorial preface to the History of Wei had long been lost; later editors patched it with excerpts from the Northern Dynasties, which itself contained lacunae that could no longer be corrected."

sentences.zh: 按「成帝世」三字，北史卷五六魏收傳無，當取他書增，據元和姓纂輯本卷八魏氏稱「漢鉅鹿太守歆，居鉅鹿」，錢氏謂成帝謂漢成帝，是。

translations.literal: According to examination, the three characters "in the reign of Emperor Cheng" are absent from the biography of Wei Shou in scroll 56 of the Northern Dynasties; they must have been added from another book. The reconstructed Yuanhe Xingzuan, scroll 8, under the Wei clan states "Xin, Administrator of Julu of Han, dwelt in Julu"; Qian's view that Emperor Cheng means Emperor Cheng of Han is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Examination shows that the phrase "in the reign of Emperor Cheng" does not appear in scroll 56 of the Northern Dynasties; it was likely added from another source. The reconstructed Yuanhe Xingzuan, scroll 8, records under the Wei clan that "Xin, Administrator of Julu under the Han, dwelt in Julu." Qian's identification of Emperor Cheng as Emperor Cheng of Han is correct.

sentences.zh: 歆子悅 北史卷五六無「歆」字。

translations.literal: "Xin's son Yue"—scroll 56 of the Northern Dynasties lacks the character "Xin."
translations.idiomatic: In "Xin's son Yue," scroll 56 of the Northern Dynasties omits the character "Xin."

sentences.zh: 按魏悅為北魏李孝伯壻，魏歆則漢成帝時人，相去四百餘年，豈得為父子。

translations.literal: According to examination, Wei Yue was son-in-law to Li Xiaobo of Northern Wei, while Wei Xin lived in the time of Emperor Cheng of Han—more than four hundred years apart; how could they be father and son?
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yue of Northern Wei was Li Xiaobo's son-in-law, while Wei Xin lived under Emperor Cheng of Han—more than four centuries apart. They cannot have been father and son.

sentences.zh: 中間世次脫簡，自宋以來即有人指出。

translations.literal: The lacuna in the intervening generations has been pointed out since the Song dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: The gap in the intervening generations has been noted since the Song dynasty.

sentences.zh: 但唐書卷七二中宰相世系表魏氏下稱歆「二子，愉、悅」，則歆有子名悅，亦有旁證。

translations.literal: Yet the Tables of Chancellors' Lineages in scroll 72 of the New Book of Tang, under the Wei clan, states that Xin "had two sons, Yu and Yue"—so Xin did have a son named Yue, and there is corroborating evidence.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Tables of Chancellors' Lineages in scroll 72 of the New Book of Tang records under the Wei clan that Xin "had two sons, Yu and Yue"—so a son named Yue is attested.

sentences.zh: 至李孝伯之壻魏悅則魏子建之父，魏收之祖，見本書卷九一王叡附王椿傳、卷九二魏溥妻房氏傳，也無可疑。

translations.literal: As for the Wei Yue who was Li Xiaobo's son-in-law, he was the father of Wei Zijian and grandfather of Wei Shou, as seen in scroll 91, biography of Wang Rui with appended biography of Wang Chun, and scroll 92, biography of the wife of Wei Pu, née Fang—there is no doubt.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Yue who was Li Xiaobo's son-in-law was father of Wei Zijian and grandfather of Wei Shou, as recorded in scroll 91 (biography of Wang Rui, with appended biography of Wang Chun) and scroll 92 (biography of Wei Pu's wife, née Fang)—and this is beyond question.

sentences.zh: 姓纂卷八和唐書世系表所著錄的後裔都是愉之後，悅的後裔無考。

translations.literal: Both the Xingzuan, scroll 8, and the Tang lineage tables record only descendants of Yu; the descendants of Yue are unverified.
translations.idiomatic: Both the Xingzuan, scroll 8, and the Tang lineage tables record only the descendants of Yu; Yue's line cannot be traced.

sentences.zh: 疑本有兩魏悅，一是西漢鉅鹿太守歆之子，一是北魏末魏子建之父。

translations.literal: It is suspected that there were originally two men named Wei Yue—one the son of Xin, Administrator of Julu of Western Han, and one the father of Wei Zijian of late Northern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: It is likely that two different men named Wei Yue were conflated—one the son of Xin, Administrator of Julu under Western Han, and one the father of Wei Zijian under late Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 由於同名，傳抄時以此悅當彼悅，脫漏中間世系。

translations.literal: Because the names were identical, in transmission one Yue was substituted for the other, and the intervening genealogy was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Because the names were identical, copyists substituted one Yue for the other and the intervening generations dropped out.

sentences.zh: 或唐初魏書已有此誤本，其誤非必出於李延壽。

translations.literal: Or the Tang-era History of Wei already had this corrupt text; the error need not necessarily originate with Li Yanshou.
translations.idiomatic: The corrupt text may already have existed in the Tang-era History of Wei; the error need not necessarily come from Li Yanshou.

sentences.zh: 初世宗時平氐 諸本「世宗」作「世祖」，北史卷五六作「宣武」

translations.literal: "Initially, in Emperor Shizong's time the Di were pacified"—in various editions "Shizong" reads "Shizu"; scroll 56 of the Northern Dynasties reads "Xuanwu"
translations.idiomatic: On "Initially, in Emperor Shizong's time the Di were pacified"—various editions read "Shizu" for "Shizong," and scroll 56 of the Northern Dynasties reads "Xuanwu"

sentences.zh: 〈即世宗元恪〉。

translations.literal: 〈that is, Emperor Shizong Yuan Ke〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈that is, Emperor Shizong Yuan Ke〉

sentences.zh: 按事見卷八世宗紀正始三年正月壬申、卷七０傅豎眼傳、卷一０一氐傳補，「祖」乃「宗」之訛，今據改。

translations.literal: According to examination, the event appears in the Annals of Emperor Shizong for the third year of Zhengshi, first month, renshen; the biography of Fu Shuyan in scroll 70; and the supplementary biography of the Di in scroll 101—"zu" is a corruption of "zong," and the text is emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: The event appears in the Annals of Emperor Shizong (Zhengshi 3, first month, renshen day), the biography of Fu Shuyan in scroll 70, and the supplementary biography of the Di in scroll 101. "Zu" is a corruption of "zong," and the text is emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 乃遣刺史唐永代焉 按刺史上無地名，不知何州刺史，據北史卷六七唐永傳但云「行臺蕭寶夤表永為南豳

translations.literal: "Then sent Regional Inspector Tang Yong to replace him"—according to examination, no place-name appears above "regional inspector"; which province is unknown. Scroll 67 of the Northern Dynasties, biography of Tang Yong, only says "Mobile Office Xiao Baoyin memorialized Yong as Regional Inspector of Southern Bin
translations.idiomatic: On "Then sent Regional Inspector Tang Yong to replace him"—no place-name appears before "regional inspector," so the province is unknown. Scroll 67 of the Northern Dynasties, biography of Tang Yong, only records that "Mobile Office Xiao Baoyin memorialized Yong as Regional Inspector of Southern Bin

sentences.zh: 〈原訛『幽』〉

translations.literal: 〈originally corrupted as "You"〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈originally corrupted as "You"〉

sentences.zh: 州刺史」，不載代魏子建事，當是省略，或北史所據唐氏家傳諱言其事。

translations.literal: Province," and does not record his replacing Wei Zijian; this must be an omission, or the family biography of the Tang clan used by the Northern Dynasties avoided mentioning the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Province," and does not mention his replacing Wei Zijian—likely an omission, or the Tang family biography used by the Northern Dynasties passed over the episode.

sentences.zh: 唐永乃由南豳遷東益，這裏「刺史」上應有「南豳州」三字。

translations.literal: Tang Yong was transferred from Southern Bin to Eastern Yi; here the three characters "Southern Bin Province" should appear above "regional inspector."
translations.idiomatic: Tang Yong was transferred from Southern Bin to Eastern Yi; the three characters "Southern Bin Province" should appear before "regional inspector" here.

sentences.zh: 吾生年契闊 北史卷五六「生年」作「平生」，這裏「生年」當是「生平」之訛。

translations.literal: "My years of life have been long and parted"—scroll 56 of the Northern Dynasties reads "throughout life" for "years of life"; here "years of life" must be a corruption of "throughout life."
translations.idiomatic: On "My years of life have been long and parted"—scroll 56 of the Northern Dynasties reads "throughout life" instead of "years of life"; "years of life" here is likely a corruption of "throughout life."

sentences.zh: 帝曰 北史卷五六「帝」上有「白」字，下文云云乃賈思同語。

translations.literal: "The emperor said"—scroll 56 of the Northern Dynasties has the character "reported" before "emperor"; the following remarks are therefore Jia Sitong's words.
translations.idiomatic: On "The emperor said"—scroll 56 of the Northern Dynasties has the character "reported" before "emperor," meaning the following remark is Jia Sitong's speech.

sentences.zh: 按御覽卷六００

translations.literal: According to examination, the Imperial Readings, scroll 600
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Readings, scroll 600,

sentences.zh: 〈二七０一頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 2701〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈page 2701〉

sentences.zh: 引北齊書也有「白」字

translations.literal: cites the History of Northern Qi and also has the character "reported"
translations.idiomatic: cites the History of Northern Qi and also has the character "reported"

sentences.zh: 〈今本北齊書無〉。

translations.literal: 〈absent from the received History of Northern Qi〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈absent from the received History of Northern Qi〉

sentences.zh: 若無「白」字，則下文云云是元恭

translations.literal: Without the character "reported," the following remarks would be those of Yuan Gong
translations.idiomatic: Without "reported," the following would be the words of Yuan Gong

sentences.zh: 〈後廢帝〉

translations.literal: 〈the Former Deposed Emperor〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈the Former Deposed Emperor〉

sentences.zh: 語，上文何必書「賈思同侍立」？

translations.literal: —so why record above that "Jia Sitong stood attending"?
translations.idiomatic: —in which case why note above that "Jia Sitong stood attending"?

sentences.zh: 這裏當脫「白」字。

translations.literal: Here the character "reported" must be missing.
translations.idiomatic: The character "reported" must have dropped out here.

sentences.zh: 博總斟酌 南、殿、局三本及北齊書卷三七「博」作「專」，百衲本、北本、汲本作「傳」；

translations.literal: "Broadly gathered and weighed"—in the Nan, Dian, and Ju editions and scroll 37 of the History of Northern Qi, "gathered" reads "devoted" and "weighed" reads "transmitted"; the Baipu, Bei, and Ji editions read "transmitted" for "gathered";
translations.idiomatic: On "Broadly gathered and weighed"—the Nan, Dian, and Ju editions and scroll 37 of the History of Northern Qi read "devoted" for "gathered" and "transmitted" for "weighed"; the Baipu, Bei, and Ji editions read "transmitted" for "gathered";

sentences.zh: 北史百衲本作「傳」，他本作「專」；

translations.literal: the Baipu edition of the Northern Dynasties reads "transmitted," other editions read "devoted";
translations.idiomatic: the Baipu edition of the Northern Dynasties reads "transmitted," while other editions read "devoted";

sentences.zh: 冊府卷五五六

translations.literal: the Cefu Yuangui, scroll 556
translations.idiomatic: the Cefu Yuangui, scroll 556

sentences.zh: 〈六六七八頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 6678〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈page 6678〉

sentences.zh: 作「博」。

translations.literal: reads "gathered."
translations.idiomatic: reads "gathered."

sentences.zh: 按「博總」即「博綜」，廣泛收集之意。

translations.literal: According to examination, "broadly gathered" means "broadly synthesized"—to collect widely.
translations.idiomatic: "Broadly gathered" means "broadly synthesized"—to collect material widely.

sentences.zh: 本作「博」，訛作「傳」，後人以「傳總」不可解，改作「專」。

translations.literal: The original read "gathered," was corrupted to "transmitted," and later men, finding "transmitted and weighed" unintelligible, changed it to "devoted."
translations.idiomatic: The original was "gathered," which was corrupted to "transmitted"; later editors, finding "transmitted and weighed" meaningless, changed it to "devoted."

sentences.zh: 今據冊府改。

translations.literal: Now emended according to the Cefu Yuangui.
translations.idiomatic: The text is now emended according to the Cefu Yuangui.
